title.zh: 中医养眼：让眼睛明亮有神的秘诀
title.en: TCM Eye Care: Secrets for Bright, Spirited Eyes

description.zh: 掌握中医养眼的方法，从调理肝肾入手，让眼睛明亮有神，告别眼部问题
description.en: Master TCM eye care methods, regulate liver-kidney for bright eyes

zh.text: 古人云："目乃心之使，神之舍。"眼睛不仅是心灵的窗户，更是脏腑精气汇聚之所。《灵枢·大惑论》曰："五脏六腑之精气，皆上注于目而为之精。"这意味着眼睛的健康状况直接反映着人体内部的脏腑功能。尤其值得关注的是，中医认为"肝开窍于目"，眼睛的视物功能、色泽和神采与肝血的充盈程度息息相关，而"肾藏精"、"肾精上注于目"又决定了眼神的明亮程度。因此，想要拥有一双明亮有神的眼眸，必须从调理肝肾这一根本入手。
中医对眼睛的认识
《黄帝内经》将眼睛与五脏六腑的关系论述得极为精辟，提出了"五脏六腑之精气皆上注于目"的整体观念。具体来说，瞳孔属肾，黑眼珠属肝，白眼珠属肺，内外眼角属心，上下眼睑属脾——这就是中医眼科著名的"五轮学说"。我在临床上发现，许多眼部问题的根源都不在眼睛本身，而在背后的脏腑失调。因此，治疗眼病和养护眼睛，绝不能头痛医头、脚痛医脚，而要从整体出发。
肝与眼睛
《素问·五脏生成》说："肝受血而能视。"肝藏血，肝血充足则上荣于目，眼睛才能视物清晰、转动灵活、神采奕奕。如果肝血不足，目失所养，最常见的表现就是眼睛干涩、视物模糊。若肝火旺盛，火性炎上，循经上攻于目，则会出现眼睛红肿、疼痛、畏光等表现。我在临床中常遇到一些长期熬夜、用眼过度的患者，面色萎黄、双目无神，究其根本就是肝血暗耗所致。调理这类患者时，养肝血永远比滴眼药水更加治本。
肾与眼睛
肾藏精，精能生髓，髓通于脑，脑为髓海，而目系上属于脑。《灵枢·海论》云："髓海不足，则脑转耳鸣，胫酸眩冒，目无所见。"肾精的盛衰直接影响着视力和眼神。肾精充足的人，眼神明亮清澈，即便到了中老年，视力依然保持良好；反之，肾精亏耗之人，往往眼神黯淡、视力早衰、过早出现老花眼或白内障。临床上我遇到不少四十岁出头就严重老花的患者，追问之下多有长期熬夜、过度劳累的经历，这正是肾精被提前透支的表现。
常见眼部问题
眼睛干涩
眼睛干涩是当代人最普遍的眼部困扰，中医认为其核心病机在于"津液不足，目失濡润"。具体而言，最常见的是肝肾阴虚型——肝血不足则泪液化生无源，肾阴亏虚则不能上滋于目。这类患者不仅眼睛干涩，还常伴有口干、腰酸、五心烦热等阴虚内热的表现。在治疗上，我常以杞菊地黄丸为基础方加减，枸杞滋补肝肾、菊花清肝明目、熟地滋阴补肾，同时配合石斛、麦冬等养阴生津之品，从源头上解决问题。
眼睛疲劳
眼睛酸胀疲劳，在中青年群体中几乎成了"标配"。其形成原因有二：一为用眼过度，耗伤肝血；二为久坐少动，气血运行不畅，目窍失养。《素问·宣明五气》曰："久视伤血。"长时间盯着屏幕，肝血持续被消耗，目失所养则酸胀不适。我在日常接诊中，遇到很多白领患者主诉"看电脑半小时就受不了"，这种情形的调理要点是补气养血配合适度休息，一味用抗疲劳眼药水只是权宜之计。
黑眼圈
黑眼圈的形成原因较为复杂，中医一般从三个方面来辨析。其一为肾虚——肾主黑色，肾精不足则眼周气血不荣，现暗沉之色，这类患者多伴有腰膝酸软、神疲乏力。其二为气血亏虚——眼睑皮肤最薄，气血不足时最先显现暗沉，多见于贫血或长期熬夜者。其三为血瘀——眼周血液循环不畅，可见青紫色黑眼圈，揉之不褪。针对不同类型的黑眼圈，调理策略截然不同：肾虚者当补肾填精，气血虚者当补益气血，血瘀者当活血通络，不可一法通治。
养眼方法
养肝明目

养肝是明目的第一要务。枸杞在《本草纲目》中被列为上品，称其"补肾益精，养肝明目"，是养眼最常用的食材，每日取15至20克嚼食或泡水，长期坚持效果显著。菊花清肝明目、疏散风热，与枸杞配伍堪称养眼"黄金搭档"。决明子在《神农本草经》中记载"主青盲，目淫肤赤白膜，眼赤痛泪出"，其清肝明目兼润肠通便的功效尤其适合伴有便秘的患者。桑叶清肺润燥、清肝明目，我在临床上常将其与菊花同用以增强清肝之力。蓝莓虽非传统中药，但其抗氧化、保护视网膜的作用已被现代研究所证实，可作为日常养眼的辅助食物。
补肾养眼
补肾是养眼的另一大支柱。黑芝麻色黑入肾，能补肝肾、益精血，《本草备要》记载其"补肝肾，润五脏，填精髓"，常食可使眼神明亮。核桃形似人脑，以形补形，补肾健脑同时亦能养眼。桑葚是春夏之交的时令佳果，滋阴补血、生津润燥，对于眼干目涩有很好的缓解作用。黑豆在《本草纲目拾遗》中被记载"补肾益精，明目"，我常建议患者将黑豆煮水代茶或煮粥食用。这些黑色食材的共同特点是入肾经、填补精血，适合长期作为养眼食疗。
养眼穴位

眼周穴位按摩是中医养护眼睛最便捷有效的方法。睛明穴位于目内眦角稍上方凹陷处，是手足太阳经、足阳明经的交会穴，通调眼部气血，是明目的第一要穴。攒竹穴在眉头内侧凹陷处，按压可缓解眼疲劳、改善眼周循环。太阳穴在眉梢与目外眦之间向后一横指凹陷处，是缓解头痛和眼疲劳的常用穴。四白穴位于眼眶下缘正中直下一横指处，《针灸甲乙经》谓其主治"目眩、目痛"，是养眼要穴。丝竹空穴在眉梢外侧凹陷处，长于缓解眼周疲劳和减少鱼尾纹。每日按揉这些穴位3至5分钟，以酸胀为度，对改善眼部气血运行大有裨益。
眼部按摩方法

眼部按摩贵在坚持，方法反而简单。我常教给患者一套"眼保健操"的改良版：用清洁的双手指腹，先以睛明穴为起点，食指和拇指配合轻轻按揉；再以拇指按揉攒竹穴，同时配合缓慢深呼吸；接着以中指指腹点按太阳穴，顺时针和逆时针各按揉18次；之后用食指指腹沿眼眶下缘从内向外轻轻推抹；最后闭目，双眼球先顺时针缓慢转动9圈，再逆时针转动9圈。全套动作约5分钟，每日早晚各做一次。坚持一段时间后，大多数患者都会反映眼睛变得轻松明亮。

zh.title: 枸杞菊花明目茶
zh.instructions:
1. 所有材料洗净
2. 加水煮沸
3. 转小火煮10分钟
4. 代茶饮用
5. 每日1次
6. 清肝明目，养眼护眼

zh.text: 消除黑眼圈方法

消除黑眼圈需要根据证型采取针对性策略，而非简单涂抹眼霜就能解决。肾虚型黑眼圈的核心在于补肾填精、充足睡眠，可多吃黑芝麻、黑豆、桑葚等黑色食物。气血亏虚型黑眼圈需要补气养血，可常食当归、红枣、桂圆，同时配合规律作息。血瘀型黑眼圈则以眼部按摩和热敷为佳，用温热的毛巾敷眼周5至10分钟，每日坚持，能有效促进眼周气血循环。无论哪种证型，规律作息、避免熬夜都是基础中的基础——晚上11点前入睡尤为重要，因为此时是肝胆经当令的时间，眠则血归于肝，有助于眼部气血的修复。
养眼生活习惯

养护眼睛是一辈子的功课。适度用眼是前提——每对着屏幕工作40至50分钟，就应远眺5至10分钟，让睫状肌得到放松。保持工作环境的湿度同样重要，空调房内可放加湿器或绿植，避免干燥加速泪液蒸发。饮食上除了上文提到的养眼食材外，深绿色蔬菜如菠菜、羽衣甘蓝富含叶黄素，对抗蓝光伤害有明确作用。最重要的是，定期休息眼睛不仅仅是"不看屏幕"，而是真正让眼睛放松——闭目养神、远眺绿色、做眼部按摩，都是极好的休息方式。
温馨提示：养眼需要长期坚持。本文所介绍的养眼方法仅供日常保健参考。如出现视力急剧下降、视物变形或眼底病变等症状，请及时到正规眼科医院就诊，以免延误治疗。

en.text: As the ancients said: "The eye is the messenger of the heart and the abode of the spirit." The eyes are not only the window to the soul but also where the essence qi of all organs converges. The Lingshu states: "The essence qi of the five zang and six fu organs all ascend to the eyes, forming the essence of vision." This means eye health directly reflects the functional state of the internal organs. Most notably, TCM holds that "the liver opens into the eyes" — visual function, brightness, and expression are intimately linked to the abundance of liver blood. The kidney stores essence, which also ascends to nourish the eyes, determining the luster of one's gaze. Therefore, to achieve bright, spirited eyes, one must begin with regulating the liver and kidney at the root.
TCM Understanding of Eyes

The Huang Di Nei Jing provides a brilliant exposition of the relationship between the eyes and the five zang organs, establishing the holistic concept that "the essence qi of all organs ascends to the eyes." Specifically, the pupil pertains to the kidney, the iris to the liver, the sclera to the lung, the inner and outer canthi to the heart, and the upper and lower eyelids to the spleen — this is the famous "five-wheel theory" of TCM ophthalmology. In my clinical experience, many eye problems originate not in the eyes themselves but in underlying organ imbalances. Therefore, treating eye conditions and maintaining eye health requires a holistic approach, never merely addressing the eyes in isolation.
Liver & Eyes

The Su Wen states: "When the liver receives blood, it can see." The liver stores blood, and when liver blood is abundant, it ascends to nourish the eyes, enabling clear vision, agile eye movement, and bright expression. When liver blood is deficient, the eyes lose nourishment, most commonly manifesting as dryness and blurred vision. Conversely, when liver fire is exuberant, its nature is to flare upward along the meridian to attack the eyes, resulting in redness, swelling, pain, and photophobia. In clinic, I frequently encounter patients who have chronically stayed up late and overused their eyes — they present with sallow complexion and dull, lifeless eyes, with the root cause being the gradual depletion of liver blood. For such patients, nourishing liver blood is always a more fundamental approach than merely using eye drops.
Kidney & Eyes

The kidney stores essence, which generates marrow. Marrow connects to the brain — the sea of marrow — and the optic system ascends to the brain. The Lingshu states: "When the sea of marrow is insufficient, there is dizziness, tinnitus, aching legs, blurred vision, and inability to see." The abundance of kidney essence directly affects visual acuity and the luster of the eyes. Those with sufficient kidney essence have bright, clear eyes and maintain good vision even into old age; conversely, those who deplete their kidney essence often present with dull eyes, early vision decline, and premature presbyopia or cataracts. In my practice, I have encountered many patients in their early forties with severe presbyopia, and upon questioning, nearly all had histories of chronic sleep deprivation and overexertion — a classic sign of prematurely depleted kidney essence.
Common Eye Problems
Dry Eyes

Dry eyes are the most common eye complaint in modern life. TCM identifies the core pathogenesis as "insufficient body fluids, eyes losing moisture." The most frequent pattern is liver-kidney yin deficiency — insufficient liver blood impairs tear production, and kidney yin deficiency prevents upward nourishment of the eyes. These patients typically also present with dry mouth, lower back soreness, and a sensation of heat in the palms and soles. In treatment, I often use modified Qi Ju Di Huang Wan as the base formula: goji berries to nourish the liver and kidney, chrysanthemum to clear the liver and brighten the eyes, prepared rehmannia to nourish kidney yin, supplemented with dendrobium and ophiopogon to nourish yin and generate fluids — addressing the problem at its source.
Eye Fatigue

Sore, fatigued eyes have become nearly universal among young and middle-aged adults. The causes are twofold: first, excessive eye use depletes liver blood; second, prolonged sitting impairs qi and blood circulation, depriving the eyes of nourishment. The Su Wen states: "Prolonged staring damages blood." Extended screen time continuously consumes liver blood, and when the eyes lose nourishment, they become sore and uncomfortable. In my daily practice, many office workers complain of being "unable to work more than thirty minutes at a computer without discomfort." For these cases, the key lies in tonifying qi and blood combined with adequate rest — relying solely on anti-fatigue eye drops is merely a temporary measure.
Dark Circles

The formation of dark circles involves several possible mechanisms, and TCM typically differentiates three patterns. The first is kidney deficiency — the kidney governs the color black, and when kidney essence is insufficient, the skin around the eyes lacks nourishment and appears dull. These patients often also have sore lower backs and general fatigue. The second is qi-blood deficiency — the eyelid skin is the thinnest on the body, making it the first area to show signs of inadequate qi and blood, commonly seen in anemia or chronic sleep deprivation. The third is blood stasis — poor circulation around the eyes produces a purplish-black hue that does not fade with pressing. Treatment strategies differ fundamentally for each type: kidney deficiency requires supplementing kidney essence, qi-blood deficiency requires fortifying qi and blood, and blood stasis requires activating blood circulation. A one-size-fits-all approach will not work.
Eye Care Methods
Nourish Liver, Brighten Eyes

Nourishing the liver is the foremost priority for bright eyes. Goji berries are classified as a top-grade herb in the Ben Cao Gang Mu, described as "tonifying the kidney and liver, nourishing the eyes and brightening vision." Taking 15 to 20 grams daily, either chewed directly or steeped as tea, yields significant results with consistent use. Chrysanthemum clears the liver and brightens the eyes while dispersing wind-heat — paired with goji berries, it forms the "golden combination" for eye care. Cassia seeds, recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as treating "blindness, eye discharge, redness, and pain," are especially suitable for patients who also suffer from constipation. Mulberry leaf clears the lung, moistens dryness, and clears the liver — in clinical practice, I combine it with chrysanthemum to enhance the liver-clearing effect. Although not a traditional Chinese herb, blueberries have been confirmed by modern research to provide antioxidant protection for the retina and can serve as a supplementary food for daily eye care.
Tonify Kidney, Care for Eyes

Tonifying the kidney is the other pillar of eye care. Black sesame, being black in color and entering the kidney meridian, nourishes the liver and kidney, and benefits essence and blood. The Ben Cao Bei Yao records it as "tonifying the liver and kidney, moistening the five viscera, and replenishing marrow" — regular consumption brightens the eyes. Walnuts, resembling the brain in shape, tonify the kidney and nourish the brain and eyes. Mulberries, the seasonal fruit of late spring and early summer, nourish yin, tonify blood, and generate fluids, providing excellent relief for dry eyes. Black beans are recorded in the Ben Cao Gang Mu Shi Yi as "tonifying the kidney, benefiting essence, and brightening the eyes" — I often recommend patients boil black bean water as tea or cook black beans in porridge. These black-colored foods share the common property of entering the kidney meridian and replenishing essence and blood, making them ideal for long-term dietary eye care.
Eye Care Acupoints

Periocular acupoint massage is the most convenient and effective method of TCM eye care. Jingming (BL1), located in the depression slightly above the inner canthus, is the meeting point of the foot taiyang and foot yangming meridians, regulating qi and blood flow to the eyes — it is the foremost acupoint for brightening vision. Cuanzhu (BL2), at the inner depression of the eyebrow, relieves eye fatigue and improves periocular circulation when pressed. Taiyang (EX-HN5), in the depression one finger-width behind the midpoint between the outer canthus and the eyebrow tail, is a common point for relieving headaches and eye strain. Sibai (ST2), directly below the pupil in the depression of the infraorbital foramen, is recorded in the Jia Yi Jing as treating "dizziness and eye pain." Sizhukong (SJ23), in the depression at the lateral end of the eyebrow, excels at relieving periocular fatigue and reducing crow's feet. Massaging these points daily for three to five minutes until a sensation of soreness and distension is achieved greatly benefits periocular qi and blood circulation.
Eye Massage Methods

Eye massage relies on consistency rather than complexity. I often teach patients an improved version of the traditional "eye exercises": using clean fingertips, begin at Jingming point, gently pressing and rubbing with the index finger and thumb. Then press Cuanzhu with the thumb while breathing slowly and deeply. Next, press Taiyang with the middle finger, rotating 18 times clockwise and 18 times counterclockwise. Following this, gently stroke along the lower orbital rim from inner to outer canthus with the index finger. Finally, close the eyes and slowly rotate the eyeballs 9 times clockwise and 9 times counterclockwise. The entire routine takes about 5 minutes and should be performed morning and evening. After consistent practice, most patients report that their eyes feel more relaxed and brighter.

en.text: Methods to Eliminate Dark Circles

Eliminating dark circles requires targeted strategies based on the specific pattern, not merely applying eye cream. For kidney deficiency-type dark circles, the core measures are supplementing kidney essence and ensuring adequate sleep — consume more black sesame, black beans, and mulberries. For qi-blood deficiency-type dark circles, tonify qi and blood with angelica, red dates, and longan, combined with a regular sleep schedule. For blood stasis-type dark circles, eye massage and warm compresses are most effective — apply a warm towel over the eye area for 5 to 10 minutes daily to promote periocular circulation. Regardless of the pattern, regular sleep and avoiding late nights are the absolute foundation — sleeping before 11 PM is especially important, as this is the time when the liver and gallbladder meridians are active, and sleep allows blood to return to the liver, facilitating periocular repair.
Eye Care Lifestyle Habits

Eye care is a lifelong practice. Moderate eye use is fundamental — every 40 to 50 minutes of screen work, look into the distance for 5 to 10 minutes to relax the ciliary muscles. Maintaining adequate humidity in your work environment is equally important — use a humidifier or keep plants in air-conditioned rooms to prevent accelerated tear evaporation from dry air. Beyond the eye-nourishing foods mentioned above, dark green vegetables such as spinach and kale are rich in lutein, which has been shown to protect against blue light damage. Most importantly, giving your eyes regular rest is not simply about "not looking at screens" — truly resting the eyes means closing them, gazing into the distance at greenery, or doing eye massage. These are all excellent forms of rest.

Note: Eye care requires long-term commitment. The methods described in this article are for daily health maintenance reference only. If you experience sudden vision decline, visual distortion, or signs of retinal pathology, please consult a qualified ophthalmologist promptly to avoid delayed treatment.
